extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Coast Guard leadership, contracting officers, policymakers, and researchers in government procurement
extracted.subtask_description: A thesis-level empirical analysis of factors causing post-award cost increases in OMB Circular A-76 contracts for U.S. Coast Guard activities, including comparisons with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) and interviews to gauge perceptions of A-76 effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award contract cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Many A-76 contracts experience cost increases after contract award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure incidence and magnitude of cost increases that occur after the contract has been awarded; use as a primary phenomenon to explain and evaluate A-76 implementation outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Labor (DOL) wage determinations ... caused cost increases (identified in earlier study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the effect of DOL wage determinations on contract cost changes; consider whether wage determinations explain observed post-award cost growth and whether contracts remain cost-effective despite these determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Added work as a cause of cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Added work caused cost increases (identified in earlier study).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and quantify additional tasks or scope increases added after award that contribute to cost growth; evaluate responsibility and mitigation options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other/additional factors causing cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze whether DOL wage determinations, added work, or additional factors caused cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically search for and evaluate other possible drivers of cost increases beyond wage determinations and added work (e.g., contract management, specifications, contractor performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison with Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract costs were compared with the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) for each activity to see if Government savings were still being realized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MEO cost estimates as the benchmark to determine whether contracting out produced net savings; compare ex post contract costs to the MEO to judge continued cost-effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: What contracting officers could do to control cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine what the Coast Guard contracting officer could do to control the cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify actionable controls, procedures, or oversight practices that contracting officers can implement to reduce likelihood or magnitude of post-award cost growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceptions of A-76 effectiveness (interview-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: To gauge USCG perceptions of the effectiveness of A-76, interviews were conducted with USCG leaders from units with 'contracted-out' commercial activities and compared with leaders from units that had the functions remaining in-house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and compare qualitative perceptions from leaders in contracted-out versus in-house units to understand acceptance, perceived benefits/shortcomings, and how perceptions correlate with measured cost outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation problems associated with perceptions of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: There are problems in the implementation of A-76 that may be associated with the perceptions of its effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify implementation shortcomings (procedural, communication, oversight, etc.) that influence stakeholders' perceptions and possibly the program's performance; link implementation issues to both perceptions and measured cost results.
